title: Restriction from the whole scheme commutes with cohomology pullback
statement: Let g:Y→X be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], W an open of X, G an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and q≥0. Let P_W be pullback along g restricted to W, followed by the coefficient identification (upperStarComp(g_W,j_W))^{-1} followed by upperStarComp(j_W_prime,g) [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Then for every x in H^q(X,G), restriction to g^{-1}W of g^*(x) equals P_W of restriction to W of x. This includes W empty, W=X, and the identity morphism. The module also abbreviates the explicitly prescribed restriction and restricted-pullback maps; it introduces no new cohomology notion.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written composition and restriction consequence.

proof.text: Apply composition functoriality to (g restricted to W) followed by W.ι, with named composite (g^{-1}W).ι ≫ g. Apply it also to (g^{-1}W).ι followed by g. The restriction identity makes the two named composites equal.

Sheaf.H.map_comp_apply identifies H^q of the composite coefficient morphisms with the composite H^q maps. The inverse comparison cancels its hom comparison since upperStarComp is an isomorphism. Apply the remaining H^q comparison to the cancellation equality; this gives the claimed square. The Lean calc explicitly writes these equalities, without any connecting map or cover assumption.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $W\subseteq X$ an open subscheme with inclusion $j_W:W\to X$, $j'_W:g^{-1}W\to Y$ the inclusion of its preimage and $g_W:g^{-1}W\to W$ the restriction of $g$, so that $j_W\circ g_W=g\circ j'_W$. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $X$ and $q\ge0$. Write $u^*:H^q(X,G)\to H^q(X',u^{-1}G)$ for the cohomology pullback along a morphism $u:X'\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], and let
$$P_W:H^q(W,j_W^{-1}G)\to H^q(g^{-1}W,j'^{-1}_Wg^{-1}G)$$
be the pullback $g_W^*$ followed by the map induced by the coefficient isomorphism $g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}G\cong(j_W\circ g_W)^{-1}G=(g\circ j'_W)^{-1}G\cong j'^{-1}_Wg^{-1}G$ given by the composition isomorphisms of inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Then for every $x\in H^q(X,G)$
$$j'^*_W\bigl(g^*x\bigr)=P_W\bigl(j_W^*x\bigr)\quad\text{in }H^q(g^{-1}W,j'^{-1}_Wg^{-1}G).$$

proof.text:
By the functoriality of cohomology pullback under composition [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], for composable $a,b$ and $c=b\circ a$ one has $a^*(b^*x)=\theta_{a,b}(c^*x)$, where $\theta_{a,b}$ is induced by the composition isomorphism $c^{-1}\cong a^{-1}b^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Apply this to $(a,b)=(g_W,j_W)$ and to $(a,b)=(j'_W,g)$; both composites are the same morphism $c=j_W\circ g_W=g\circ j'_W:g^{-1}W\to X$. Thus
$$g_W^*(j_W^*x)=\theta_{g_W,j_W}(c^*x),\qquad j'^*_W(g^*x)=\theta_{j'_W,g}(c^*x).$$
Since $\theta_{g_W,j_W}$ is induced by an isomorphism, applying the map induced by its inverse to the first identity gives $c^*x$, and then applying $\theta_{j'_W,g}$ gives $j'^*_W(g^*x)$. By definition of $P_W$ (and since cohomology of a composite of coefficient maps is the composite of the induced maps) this composite is $P_W(j_W^*x)$.
